decisions.text: type bar: categories compared by value

an outlier inset: Northgate Museum & Art Gallery (1840) dwarfs the others (at most 142.3), and the small values must be compared (facts.small_values_matter); the full scale from zero kept, and Harbour Maritime Museum, Castle Keep & Grounds, Hartley Museum of Textiles, Victoria Mill Engine House, Ropewalk Folk Museum, St Bede's Chapel & Undercroft, Lowfield Tram Depot, Weavers' Cottages and Old Grammar School Gallery re-plotted on their own scale from zero, 0–150 by 50 (G2.26)
nominal categories sorted by value, descending

“Northgate Museum & Art Gallery” and “Harbour Maritime Museum” come within 10 pt of each other under vertical bars, with every multi-word name wrapped: horizontal bars, names right-aligned at the left
labels as a set, 0 decimals, bare numbers: 0, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000
digits hidden: thousands, stated in the scale's title (R2-05, D-3): “Visits counted at the door (thousands)”
the names' column widened to 150 pt (41% of the width, at most 50%), so that Northgate Museum & Art Gallery stands on one line and fewer wrapped names crowd their neighbours
a horizontal scale: bare numbers, and its title centred below with the unit in parentheses: “Visits counted at the door (thousands)”

no empty area of the plot holds the inset: it stands beside the members' bars, on their rows, the two charts sharing the names at the left (space is short: one combined chart, labelled once; owner, 30 Sep 2026); the main plot runs 27 pt on under its last row to hold the inset's scale
the inset beside the members' bars, on their rows, under the outliers' bars

the inset's form: a frame round the bars of Harbour Maritime Museum, Castle Keep & Grounds, Hartley Museum of Textiles, Victoria Mill Engine House, Ropewalk Folk Museum, St Bede's Chapel & Undercroft, Lowfield Tram Depot, Weavers' Cottages and Old Grammar School Gallery, a larger frame round a complete small chart (0–150 by 50, its unit in its title (“Visits counted at the door (thousands)”), no category or time labels of its own, the main chart's axis serving both, no title, text at inset size), two links forming a widening cone, beneath the frames (G2.27)

findings.message: scale.magnitude thousands departs from the procedure, which gives millions (digits hidden from five integer digits, by the largest unit needing at most one decimal (R5-10, D-4))
findings.reason: the inset's scale is in thousands; the same magnitude on the main scale lets the panel read both scales as one set of numbers
findings.title: large magnitudes stated once, not as trailing zeros

source.shows: an outlier inset at the text width (eval round 1, B06): no empty area of the plot holds the small chart with its own names, so it stands beside the members' bars, on their rows, sharing the names (the owner's exception for an aligned inset when space is short); wide, at 480 pt, the inset in the plot's empty area with its names repeated; ascending, the members above the outlier: nothing holds the inset, which is not drawn, with a warning
